EXPLANATION

The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=a is given by P4(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+f(4)(a)4!(x−a)4.

Here, we have a=1, so P4(x)=f(1)+f′(1)(x−1)+f″(1)2!(x−1)2+f‴(1)3!(x−1)3+f(4)(1)4!(x−1)4.

So we need to work out f(1), f′(1), f″(1), f‴(1) and f(4)(1), as follows: f(x)=x5/3⟹f(1)=15/3=1f′(x)=53x2/3⟹f′(1)=53f″(x)=109x−1/3⟹f″(1)=109f‴(x)=−1027x−4/3⟹f‴(1)=−1027f(4)(x)=4081x−7/3⟹f(4)(1)=4081

Therefore, P4(x) is given by P4(x)=1+53(x−1)+109⋅2!(x−1)2−1027⋅3!(x−1)3+4081⋅4!(x−1)4=1+53(x−1)+59(x−1)2−581(x−1)3+5243(x−1)4.
